$comment: Adjudicated corrections applied over the upstream NeuroInject bundle at conversion time.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The corpus is generated from an external bundle, so hand-editing
content/tools/neuroinject.json would be erased by the next import. These corrections are
not edits to the source; they are an overlay with provenance, applied by
scripts/convert_neuroinject.mjs after the source is read.
HOW A CORRECTION IS STRUCTURED. `muscle` and `field` locate the string. `find` must match
the CURRENT upstream text exactly. `replace` is the adjudicated wording. `source` is the
citation that justifies it, and `why` states the defect in one line.
THE GATE THAT MATTERS. If `find` no longer matches anything, the build FAILS. Every failure
this audit uncovered was silent - a mirrored scalar, a copied field, an arithmetic column -
and the repair must not add another. If upstream rewrites a string we corrected, someone
has to look at it rather than have the overlay quietly miss.
Set `replace` to null to DELETE a string outright (used where a claim is wrong and has no

FORBID. A correction may carry `forbid`: phrases that must not appear ANYWHERE in that muscle's text after the overlay runs. This exists because the first pass corrected the subclavian-artery inversion in ultrasound.safetyNotes and left an identical claim standing in placement, so the page contradicted itself. Correcting one field is not correcting the claim.

TIERS. 1 = precise, false and actionable at the needle. 2 = scanning fields: probe site, level or depth against motor-point and injection-technique literature. Both are applied identically; the tier is for triage, not behaviour.

OPERATIONS. A correction is a REPLACE by default (`find` + `replace`). `op: "add"` appends `text` to `field` instead, creating the field if absent — used for tier 4, which supplies hazards the corpus never had rather than fixing ones it got wrong.

SIDE EFFECTS vs PROCEDURE COMPLICATIONS. `sideEffects` is a field this overlay creates. It holds what the TOXIN does: the function lost when the target is weakened as intended, and the weakness caused when it spreads to a neighbour. `dangerZones` and `ultrasound.safetyNotes` hold what the NEEDLE can hit. The corpus only ever had the second kind, which is why in several records the primary clinical risk of the injection was absent from both hazard layers.
Full audit and the 167-entry correction queue: .research/MASTER/

corrections.why: Inverts a safety-critical vascular relationship: names the plane deep to the anterior scalene as if the artery were elsewhere.
corrections.find: The subclavian artery passes anterior to the anterior scalene at its inferior extent, and the vertebral artery lies within the transverse foramina deep to the scalenes — always use color Doppler to identify these vessels before injecting.
corrections.replace: The subclavian ARTERY passes POSTERIOR to the anterior scalene, through the scalene triangle with the brachial plexus — the plane deep to the anterior scalene is not a safe plane. The subclavian VEIN is the vessel that passes anterior to it. The vertebral artery lies within the transverse foramina, deep and medial. Use color Doppler to identify all three before injecting.

corrections.why: Names the hazard's location and offers it as the safe zone. The common peroneal nerve wraps the fibular NECK, roughly 2 cm distal to the head.
corrections.find: The common peroneal nerve wraps around the proximal fibula — stay distal to the fibular head.
corrections.replace: The common peroneal nerve wraps the fibular NECK, about 2 cm distal to the fibular head — so "distal to the head" is where the nerve is, not a safe zone. Stay medial to the fibula and identify the nerve on the image before advancing.

corrections.why: Backwards. The spinal accessory nerve lies between trapezius and levator scapulae, so the recommended path goes straight through it.
corrections.find: The spinal accessory nerve crosses the posterior triangle superficial to the levator scapulae — deep injection through the trapezius helps avoid this nerve, but be aware of its course if injecting the superior cervical portion of the muscle.
corrections.replace: The spinal accessory nerve runs in the plane BETWEEN trapezius and levator scapulae, so a needle driven deep through trapezius passes through the nerve's plane rather than avoiding it. Identify the nerve on the image and approach outside it; depth through trapezius is not protective.
forbid: deep injection through the trapezius helps avoid

corrections.why: The femoral nerve is extramuscular, in the fascia iliaca compartment on the anterior face of the muscle - directly in an anterior needle's path, not safely inside a cleft.
corrections.find: CRITICAL: The femoral nerve runs WITHIN the iliopsoas complex, in the groove between iliacus (lateral) and psoas major (medial). It is NOT simply medial to iliopsoas. Identify it as a hyperechoic honeycomb structure and direct the needle to the muscle belly away from this cleft.
corrections.replace: CRITICAL: The femoral nerve lies OUTSIDE the muscle, in the fascia iliaca compartment between the fascia iliaca and the epimysium of iliopsoas — on the muscle's anterior face, directly in the path of an anterior needle. Identify it as a hyperechoic honeycomb structure before the needle crosses the fascia iliaca, and approach from lateral to it.

corrections.why: 2-4 cm is past the deep fascia and into soleus. The medial belly measures 13.25 +/- 1.86 mm under a median 2.3 mm of fat.
corrections.find: Injection depth: 2-4 cm, depending on muscle thickness.
corrections.replace: Injection depth: about 0.5-1.5 cm from the skin. The medial belly averages only ~1.3 cm thick at the injection site under ~2-3 mm of fat — set depth on the ultrasound image and stop short of the deep fascia.

corrections.why: Same summary line, same defect. The lateral head is the thinner of the two at 10.84 +/- 1.52 mm.
corrections.find: Injection depth: 2-4 cm, depending on muscle thickness.
corrections.replace: Injection depth: about 0.5-1.2 cm from the skin. The lateral belly is the thinner head, ~1.1 cm at the injection site — measure it on ultrasound before advancing.

corrections.why: Instructs a 2 cm margin from a landmark the nerve has been measured 20.7 +/- 1 mm from, and found as close as 14 mm to. The margin names the nerve's position.
corrections.find: The injection site is in the center of the lateral gastrocnemius belly, 2-3 cm distal to the popliteal crease, well medial to the fibular head. Maintain at least 2 cm of clearance from the fibular head to avoid the common peroneal nerve.
corrections.replace: The injection site is in the center of the lateral gastrocnemius belly, well medial to the fibula. Do NOT rely on a fixed distance from the fibular head — the nerve crosses the fibular neck and has been found as close as 14 mm to the head. Identify the nerve on the image and keep the needle medial to it.

corrections.why: The landmark is unsupported and incoherent - a point above the scapular spine is not in the posterior triangle. Depth is also the wrong protection: the nerve lies ~3 mm deep.
corrections.find: The spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) runs on the deep surface of the upper trapezius, approximately 2-3 cm above the scapular spine in the posterior triangle of the neck — avoid deep injections in this zone and use the minimum effective dose to preserve voluntary shoulder elevation.
corrections.replace: The spinal accessory nerve runs on the deep surface of the upper trapezius, entering the muscle a mean of about 5 cm above the clavicle, referenced to the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid rather than to the scapular spine. In the posterior triangle it lies only about 3 mm below the skin, so depth does not protect it — position does. Stay in the medial half of the upper trapezius and use the minimum effective dose to preserve voluntary shoulder elevation.

corrections.why: The same inverted vessel claim corrected in safetyNotes also lives here. Correcting one field left the record contradicting itself on the page.
corrections.find: CRITICAL: Ultrasound guidance is MANDATORY for scalene injection — the brachial plexus roots pass between the anterior and middle scalenes (interscalene groove), and the subclavian artery passes anterior to the anterior scalene. The phrenic nerve runs on the anterior surface of the anterior scalene.
corrections.replace: CRITICAL: Ultrasound guidance is MANDATORY for scalene injection — the brachial plexus roots pass between the anterior and middle scalenes (interscalene groove), and the subclavian ARTERY passes POSTERIOR to the anterior scalene, through the scalene triangle with the plexus. The subclavian VEIN is the vessel anterior to it. The phrenic nerve runs on the anterior surface of the anterior scalene.
